risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: Glencore's industrial and marketing earnings are highly sensitive to copper, cobalt, zinc, nickel, coal and oil prices. The 2024 AR flags commodity price volatility as a principal risk; coal price normalization materially compressed EBITDA.
risks.summary: Sharp moves in mined and traded commodity prices directly impact mining margins and marketing arbitrage profitability, with high operating leverage on industrial assets.

risks.title: Geopolitical and Country Risk
risks.score_rationale: Significant operations in DRC, Kazakhstan, Colombia, Bolivia and other higher-risk jurisdictions. Resource nationalism, export bans (e.g. cobalt), license renewals and sanctions exposure are repeatedly cited as principal risks.
risks.summary: Operations and offtake exposed to expropriation, contract revisions, export restrictions and sanctions in higher-risk jurisdictions could disrupt production and impair assets.

risks.title: Compliance, Bribery and Legacy Investigations
risks.score_rationale: Following the 2022 US/UK/Brazil bribery and market manipulation settlements (~USD 1.5bn), Glencore remains under DPA monitoring with ongoing related civil claims and Swiss/Dutch investigations disclosed in the AR.
risks.summary: Residual exposure from past bribery and market manipulation cases, ongoing monitorships and related civil litigation could result in additional fines, debarment and reputational harm.

risks.title: Health, Safety and Environmental Risk
risks.score_rationale: Underground and open-pit mining, smelting and coal operations carry inherent fatality, tailings dam and pollution risks. The 2024 AR reports fatalities and identifies catastrophic hazards (tailings, ground failure).
risks.summary: Mining fatalities, tailings dam failures, smelter incidents or environmental contamination could trigger production halts, remediation costs and legal liability.

risks.title: Climate Transition and Coal Run-off
risks.score_rationale: Glencore's strategy to run down its coal portfolio while expanding transition metals exposes it to carbon regulation, financing pressure from institutional investors and stranded-asset risk if rundown accelerates.
risks.summary: Tightening carbon regulation, divestment pressure on coal and uncertainty over copper/cobalt transition demand could impair asset values and limit financing options.

risks.title: Marketing Trading and Counterparty Risk
risks.score_rationale: The marketing segment runs significant trading books with VaR limits; counterparty default, mark-to-market losses or working capital squeezes during commodity dislocations are principal risks.
risks.summary: Counterparty defaults, margin call spikes or trading losses in the marketing book could materially impact earnings and require additional liquidity.
